title: Result of a memory command, format 1
description: The JSON object that every command of the memory skill prints. See memory.md, Commands of the memory skill.

command.description: The command's name; none when the command is missing or unknown, with the code usage.

say.description: One or two sentences in English, which the agent tells the user in the user's language.

data.description: What the command found or changed; its fields depend on the command and the code.

confirm.description: With the outcome confirm only: the code that the same command takes with --confirm after the user's yes.

any-command-codes.description: The codes that a command can have whatever it is, whose data is data-any.

argument.description: An argument as given, such as an item ID.

error.description: A code of the error lists, a provider's error type or an exception's class name; never an error's text.

range.description: A start and an end in an entry's text, as TBL-007 counts them.

keys.description: Whether each memory key is in the environment, and whether its API rejected it.

list-line.description: A line of the item list (TBL-015).

matches.description: With item-not-found: the closest lines of the item list.

data-any.description: The data of a result whose code is one of any-command-codes.

field.description: With configuration-invalid: the first field or environment variable that fails, such as retention.days or CORTHEX_MEMORY_HOME.

clash.description: With not-in-project: the projects that each hold the folder.

error.description: With internal: the class of the error.

consent.description: When it asks: the consent text that the user says yes to.

data-status.description: The memory status (SPEC-033): no conversation text and no key.

folder.description: The memory store's folder, with the home folder written as ~.

field.description: When it is not valid: the first field or environment variable that fails.

needed.description: The consent version that the release needs.

given.description: The version the user consented to, if any.

test_servers.description: The APIs for which a test server is set.

usage.description: This month's usage, from the usage log.

cost.description: In US dollars, by the price lists named in the usage lines.

unpriced.description: Models that the price list does not name; their calls count 0.

failures.description: The most recent lines of the failure log, newest first.

hooks.description: The hook timings of the last 7 days, one entry per hook and host that ran.

waits.description: What waits for consent or a key.

unreadable.description: The parts left out because their files cannot be read.

oldest.description: When the oldest unprocessed turn was written.

pins.description: The pinned items, in the order they were pinned.

failure.description: A line of the failure log (TBL-004).

last.description: When the hook last ran in the host.

outcomes.description: Runs by outcome; no-answer counts the turns that ended without a final answer, and lock-busy the entries skipped.

failures.description: The failed attempts that the stop came from.

items.description: Lines of the item list, newest first.

more.description: The number of lines left out by --limit.

by.description: words, or both for words and meaning.

reason.description: Why it searched by words only.

results.description: Items of every status, best first.

missing.description: With item-not-found: the arguments that name no item of the project.

held.description: here: this device's raw log holds the entry; deleted: this device wrote it and it is gone; elsewhere: another device wrote it.

before.description: With --around: the entry's text before the quote.

after.description: With --around: the entry's text after the quote.

pins.description: The pinned items afterwards, or with pin-no-room the pinned items now.

current.description: With item-not-current: the current item at the end of the superseded item's replacements, when there is one.

also.description: Other items that quote the same raw text and stay unless named with --with.

state_lines.description: The current state lines that go.

pinned.description: The items forgotten that are pinned.

raw.description: This device's raw log entries whose quoted text is replaced, and the ranges kept whole for an item that stays.

missing.description: With item-not-found: the arguments that name no item of the project.

history_records.description: History records removed or with a nonempty reason cleared, counting each once; already-empty surviving reasons are excluded.

sync.description: on: a project tombstone goes to the sync remote.

left.description: With files-left: the files that could not be deleted, relative to the memory store.

folder.description: The memory store's folder, with the home folder written as ~.

projects.description: null when the full project list cannot be verified.

items.description: null when this count cannot be verified.

entries.description: null when this count cannot be verified.

usage.description: Lines of all usage logs; null when the count cannot be verified.

sync.description: on: remote and other devices keep their copies; unknown: sync state cannot be verified.

left.description: With files-left: the files that could not be deleted, relative to the memory store.

kinds.description: The kinds of entries left out, afterwards.

outside.description: With folder-outside: the folders given that are outside the project.

entries.description: When it asks: the entries that the next session start deletes.

pulled.description: With now: the items that the merge added or changed.

other.description: With other-files: up to 20 paths in the sync branch that are not memory's.

at.description: The project's folder on the temporary device.

script.description: The setup script: POSIX shell, holding no key.

device.description: Once done, the new device ID; with nothing to repair, the store record's.

items.description: Short reasons read locally from line history, at most 200 UTF-8 bytes each.

binding.description: SHA-256 of the relevant run, revisions, dependencies, privacy markers and history snapshot, required for undo confirmation previews.

phase.description: Asking: where the migration starts; nothing: complete or format-2; done: migrated; with migration-stopped: where the next run resumes, when known.

resumed.description: Once done: the phase that this run resumed; absent for a fresh migration.

release.description: The plugin release that the migrated store records.

binding.description: Asking: the lowercase SHA-256 of the store folder, the phase and its record, the named headers and the configuration copies that the confirmation binds.

reason.description: With migration-blocked: why the store cannot be migrated now; unsupported-release means the C1 release that made the store, or the running release, is not one this migration supports. With migration-stopped: why the run stopped, when known; deadline means the operation deadline passed, and store-changed means the store, its configuration or the confirmed facts changed after the migration began.
